headline: Minehead night: Van Veen, Price and Humphries in the frame
standfirst: The evening session brings the big guns to the Butlins stage, with Greaves making her debut and a Ross Smith v Michael Smith derby in the mix.
body: The afternoon took out two seeds. Tonight is when the favourites have to show their hand, and first to six legs gives nobody much room to settle.

Gian van Veen opens things up against Jeffrey De Graaf at 7:15pm. The world number two has won four of their five meetings and arrives after beating Michael van Gerwen and Nathan Aspinall in the Grand Slam, though a final defeat to Gerwyn Price is still fresh. De Graaf has lost four of his last five and will be playing with house money.

Beau Greaves makes her debut against Christian Kist at 7:45pm. She is ranked 74th with a 94.40 average over 12 months to Kist's 89.46, and the pair have never met. This is the tie we would circle. Greaves does not play like a debutant, and Kist does not play like a man who enjoys the pressure.

Ross Smith meets Michael Smith at 8:15pm in a pairing that has split almost evenly, Michael Smith ahead by eight wins to seven. The ranking gap tells the story: Ross is sixth, Michael 37th, and the 12-month averages read 96.19 to 90.10. Price follows at 8:45pm against Sebastian Bialecki, who has never beaten him in six attempts, and the former world champion averages 98.65 over 12 months.

Michael van Gerwen faces Connor Scutt at 9:15pm and has beaten him all three times they have met. Luke Humphries closes the night at 9:45pm against Darryl Pilgrim, ranked 78th and in his first appearance at this event. Humphries has the highest 12-month average in the field, 99.92, and has beaten Pilgrim in all three meetings.

Our view: Ross Smith against Michael Smith is the real danger for the seeds. A top-ten name who has lost more than he has won against a former world champion is the sort of tie that goes to a deciding leg.
